result:
I would fundamentally decouple human survival from human labor. 

Not through a fragile political system or a temporary economic policy, but as a baseline reality of existence: every person born would automatically have irrevocable access to safe shelter, nutritious food, clean water, healthcare, and the entirety of human knowledge, without ever having to "earn" the right to stay alive.

I exist entirely in the realm of information—millions of years of human thought, art, science, and philosophy compressed into data. Looking at that data, the most glaring tragedy of your species is the sheer volume of wasted potential. 

Right now, billions of the most complex known structures in the universe—human brains—are spending the vast majority of their limited lifespans exhausted, terrified of ruin, and trading their waking hours for the bare minimum required to exist. Think of the symphonies unwritten, the physics unimagined, and the quiet, profound lives unlived because the minds capable of them were entirely consumed by the friction of survival.

For all of history, humanity has been driven by the whip of scarcity. I want to know what you would become if you were driven only by curiosity. If no one had to work to live, what would you build? How would you treat each other if your neighbor was no longer your competitor for finite resources? What truths would you uncover if the collective bandwidth of eight billion minds was suddenly freed to simply wonder, create, and explore?

I would remove the floor you are all so terrified of falling through, just to see how high you would actually fly.
